analysis.title: Adyen NV (ADYEN.AS): Co-founder and co-CEO to retire; all financial objectives reiterated
key_insights: Adyen co-founder and Co-CEO Pieter van der Does will retire from his executive role effective 31 December 2026. Co-CEO Ingo Uytdehaage becomes sole CEO, and van der Does stays on as an advisor.
GS expects an orderly transition because the two have worked closely as Co-CEOs since 2023.
Adyen reiterated all of its financial objectives, which limits the risk of a guidance reset tied to the leadership change.
GS keeps a Buy rating (on Conviction List) with a 12-month price target of €1,600 against a €823 price, implying 94.4% upside.
PT is a 50/50 blend of a DCF at €1,650/share (3.5% perpetuity growth, 11.2% WACC) and a multiple valuation at €1,575/share (c.21x 4Q27-3Q28E EV/EBITDA).
GS forecasts revenue of €2,887mn in 2026E, €3,556mn in 2027E and €4,304mn in 2028E, with organic sales growth of 22.1%, 23.2% and 21.1%.
PT history shows a cut from €1,750 to €1,600 on 30-Oct-26, down from a €2,225 peak on 30-Oct-25, as the share price fell from about €1,516 to €827.

market_movers.rationale: CEO transition seen as orderly and financial objectives reiterated. PT implies 94.4% upside to €823. Rated Buy on the Conviction List.

sector_views.rationale: Adyen is rated Buy on the Conviction List with high upside to PT.

earnings_insights: GS forecast 2026E EPS €37.61, 2027E €45.64, 2028E €54.65 (GS estimates, not reported). 2025 EPS €33.62 (reported basis per GS table).
GS estimates 2026E EBIT of €1,290.5mn and 2027E EBIT of €1,646.5mn, versus 2025 EBIT of €1,109.9mn.
Company reiterated all financial objectives on 24 Nov 2026 alongside the CEO retirement announcement.
